title: Paloma and the Inheritance
premise: True-crime podcaster Isandro Marchetti is hired by a nervous woman named Paloma Vidal, who insists that her estranged aunt's death in the coastal town of Serra Brava was staged — not to cover up a murder, but to fake one, so that someone can be framed for it later. Digging into the closed case, Isandro discovers the 'victim' may still be alive and that Paloma herself is the designated scapegoat, tied to an inheritance she never wanted. As the real conspirators close in, Isandro must expose the staged death before Paloma is arrested for a murder that never happened. The story ends with the truth aired on his podcast, the inheritance dissolved into a trust for the town's found-family community, and Paloma — orphaned twice over — finally belonging somewhere.
about_author: Orsen Almeida is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing other people's worst days before turning them into fiction. He lives near the Atlantic coast and writes mysteries about the stories towns agree to forget.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Fresh off solving his third 'accident,' Isandro receives a thick envelope of cash from Paloma Vidal with one strange request: prove her aunt Beatriz's death last year was murder — before another body turns up. The beat is intrigue laced with unease; he takes the case against his better judgment.

chapters.title: The Town That Closed Its Eyes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In Serra Brava, everyone repeats the same script: Beatriz fell from the cliff path, case closed. But the police report has gaps, and the local constable flinches at Beatriz's name. The emotional beat is isolation — Isandro feels the town's silence pressing down like weather.

chapters.title: Paloma's Version
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Flashback chapters of letters: Paloma grew up in Beatriz's house until a family rupture sent her away at sixteen. She reveals the will — everything goes to her, which makes her the perfect suspect. The beat is longing; she wants the truth but fears what it costs.

chapters.title: A Death Without a Body
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Exhumation paperwork stalls; the coffin's weight record doesn't match its contents list. Isandro realizes the impossible: there may be no body because there was no death. The beat is vertigo — the case inverts beneath him.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper Who Waited
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, mostly the housekeeper Rosa. Rosa kept Beatriz's garden alive for a year after the funeral — because someone still eats the figs left on the sill. Her quiet loyalty cracks the town's silence open. The beat is tenderness hiding terror.

chapters.title: Three Names on the Will
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The original will named three heirs; two were quietly removed weeks before the 'death.' Both now live comfortably abroad, funded by monthly transfers. Someone bought their silence. The beat is cold anger as the conspiracy takes shape.

chapters.title: What the Cliff Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma returns to the cliff path and recovers a buried cache: Beatriz's own notes predicting her staged death, naming her brother Aurelio as the architect. Paloma realizes she was never hired to find the truth — she was bait. The beat is betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Frame
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Aurelio's allies plant evidence linking Paloma to a fresh break-in at the house; the constable who once flinched now moves to arrest her. Isandro records everything, realizing the only safe place for the evidence is broadcast. The beat is a race against a closing trap.

chapters.title: Episode One Hundred
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Isandro airs the centennial episode live from Serra Brava as Aurelio tries to silence him; Rosa testifies, the removed heirs confess by phone, and Beatriz herself steps out of hiding to face her brother. The beat is catharsis — the town forced to hear what it chose not to see.

chapters.title: Figs on the Sill
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With Aurelio charged and the inheritance frozen into a community trust restoring Beatriz's house as a home for displaced families, Paloma chooses to stay. She leaves figs on the windowsill out of habit, then out of hope. The final beat is belonging — found family, built where the lie used to live.
